subject: Sandbox variant pin request and compatibility path for sylph-2.1-small

Subject: Sandbox variant request: sylph-2.1-small

Marcus —

We discovered a compatibility delta between sylph-2.1-small and our downstream tokenization assumptions while prepping the ACME demo. The model's new tokenizer merges common retail SKUs differently and that causes entity extraction regressions in a handful of flows (see compat-diff.txt). QA reproduced on staging with our integration suite.

Request: can we pin the sandbox route used by ACME to the previous compatible variant (sylph-2.0.12) while we surface fixes, and run a short compatibility gating run for sylph-2.1-small? Product needs a clear timeline because ACME's POC demo is next Thursday.

Key asks:
- Quick compatibility check from infra/dev — how hard is a pin in sandbox vs staging?
- Risk assessment (latency, tokenization drift, hallucination risk)
- A rollback/fallback plan if we see >2% extraction delta

Attachments: sylph-2.1-release-notes.pdf, compat-diff.txt

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Intake
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox variant request: sylph-2.1-small

Quick technical summary from the compat run we just started:

Findings (preliminary):
- Tokenizer change: sylph-2.1 introduced an aggressive subword merge for alpha-numeric tokens; this affects SKU boundary detection.
- Embedding drift: average cosine change ~0.04 on our SKU sample set — notable but not catastrophic.
- Latency: no material change in p50/p95.

Workplan & estimates:
- Short-term (today/overnight): pin ACME sandbox route to sylph-2.0.12 — trivial config toggle, ~10–30m to deploy and validate.
- Mid-term (24–72h): run A/B in staging (5% traffic) with sylph-2.1-small, collect extraction delta and hallucination heuristics using existing eval harness.
- Migration: we can run a tokenizer-alignment script that rewrites a small normalization table (migration-script.patch) — low risk, ~1 engineer day to validate.

Risks:
- If ACME ingestion relies on the new tokenization for dedupe, we could see functional mismatch post-migration. Recommend conservative pin in sandbox and staged A/B testing.

I've attached compat-runbook.md and migration-script.patch. I'll push the pin to sandbox once I get Marcus' approval to proceed.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox variant request: sylph-2.1-small

Thanks for the quick triage. Approved with constraints:

1) Sandbox-only pin: limit the pin to ACME's sandbox route and label the change with expiration = 48 hours by default.
2) Telemetry gate: run the A/B in staging for 24–48h; require a redline metric for rollback if extraction delta > 2% OR hallucination signals increase above baseline by 1.5x.
3) Automatic fallback: implement an automated fallback to sylph-2.0.12 if the redline is triggered.
4) Cost/latency: include a short note on any expected cost delta before finalizing.
5) Security: Grace, confirm whether supplied SKU samples are PII-free; if not, we need a data handling exception and logging controls.

If the above are met, proceed and update me with the staging A/B dashboard link. Keep the pin window as short as possible.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform & Reliability
Redwood Inference

2) Kick off a 24h A/B in staging (5% traffic) with telemetry dashboards attached; evaluate extraction delta and hallucination heuristics.

5) Grace: confirm PII status of ACME samples and sign off on log retention and masking.
